subject: Help with mixed effects model with ar1 term on intercepts

messages.author: 32bf4f27a31a68db
messages.subject: Help with mixed effects model with ar1 term on intercepts
parts:
Hello,

I'm new to INLA, coming from using both LME4 and Stan.  INLA looks very promising for my research, as it is significantly faster than Stan.  (Stan can take several days to run my more complex models, and that kills any advanced model development and testing.)


The model is a longitudinal study that has both fixed and random effects.  There are between 1 and 50 repeated measures for around 1000 individuals.

Fitting a per-individual intercept is simple, and the subsequent model fit is reasonably good:
score ~ factor1 + factor2 + f(rand_eff_1, model="iid") + f(person_id, model="iid")


However, I've noticed that a person''s score will change over time.  So I'd like to try an AR1 for each person.

(Additionally, the score can have some curvature to it.  The score will improve over time, reach a peak, then slowly decline.  But, I'm not sure if this is too complicated to model with INLA.)


What would be a good way to model the per-person intercept in a way that also includes the AR1 term?

Any and all suggestions would be greatly appreciated!

Thank You,

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Help with mixed effects model with ar1 term on intercepts
parts:
On Tue, 2018-12-11 at 22:51 -0800, Bayes2 wrote:
> score ~ factor1 + factor2 + f(rand_eff_1, model="iid") + f(person_id,
> model="iid")
>
>
> However, I've noticed that a person''s score will change over time.
> So I'd like to try an AR1 for each person.

that would typically be something like

f(time, model="ar1", replicate = person_id)

giving one AR1 process for each person with the same hyperparameters.
person_id = 1, 2, 3,....

you know how to proceed like this?



--
Håvard Rue

Thank Havard,

That's helpful.

If I understand the format correctly, this sill generate a coefficient (for time) for each person. 

If I also want an intercept, would it be correct to write:
data$person_id2 <- data$person
f(time, model="ar1", replicate=person_id) + f(person_id2, model="iid")

Separately, I've seen a different format, but don't understand what it does
f(person_id, time, model="iid")
or
f(person_id, time, model="ar1")

Is there a good tutorial or documentation about all the things we can do with f()?  I've seen many examples, but not clear docs.

Thank You!
